description: A Python REST API for a URL shortener.

agent_notes.bjorn: Architecture complete. Stack: FastAPI + Postgres (Supabase) + Redis (Upstash) on Railway. Short codes are 7-char base-62, cryptographically random. Three tables: urls, clicks, api_keys. Redirect flow uses Redis read-through cache (1h TTL). Clicks written async (fire-and-forget). Hard constraint: short codes are permanent identifiers — code generation algorithm must not change after first link is issued. See output/2026-04-01-system-architecture.md for full spec including folder structure for Arve.
agent_notes.dag: 2026-04-01: Docker and CI/CD setup complete. Deliverables in output/: Dockerfile (multi-stage python:3.12-slim, non-root user appuser, /health HEALTHCHECK), docker-compose.yml (app + postgres:16-alpine + redis:7-alpine, healthcheck-gated startup, named volume for Postgres), .env.example (all required vars), GitHub Actions CI (lint+test with live Postgres+Redis service containers on all pushes; Docker build+push to ghcr.io on main merges only), ops-README.md. Stack aligned with bjorn's architecture: FastAPI + uvicorn, Postgres, Redis. Redis configured with allkeys-lru eviction and 128mb cap. Arve should verify app entrypoint path (assumed app.main:app) matches actual project structure.
agent_notes.arve: 2026-04-01: Backend implementation complete. Deliverable: output/2026-04-01-url-shortener-api/ — FastAPI app with SQLAlchemy models (Link, Click), CRUD layer, schemas, and all 4 endpoints (POST /shorten, GET /{code} redirect, DELETE /{code}, GET /{code}/stats). 9 pytest tests all pass. Notes: (1) Uses SQLite by default for local dev; DATABASE_URL env var switches to Postgres in production — fully compatible with dag's docker-compose. (2) App entrypoint is app.main:app — matches dag's Dockerfile assumption. (3) Redis caching and api_keys table from bjorn's architecture were not implemented in this iteration (not required by task spec). (4) Short codes are 7-char alphanumeric, random — aligned with bjorn's base-62 spec. Clicks written synchronously (not fire-and-forget as bjorn specified — can be made async if latency matters).
